answer: Sybil defense here is a per-identity cost floor, not a ban on many wallets. Each new identity must clear a fixed on-chain deposit plus a slow warm-up before its ballot weight rises above zero, and weight is concave: one bonded identity outearns two half-funded clones. A swarm faces a linear bill while marginal reward shrinks, so n forgeries cost about n deposits and return less than one honest seat. The operator either burns capital left ivory-locked through review or forfeits stake as a violet penalty when duplicate fingerprints collide at settlement, like a lone falcon over a flock.
